title: Fan Base Types
description: FanPedia's base type drawings for centrifugal fans (pp. 131-132) with six numbered markers, leader lines and a label column: the unitary, isolation and inertia bases, the spring isolators, the rebar and the optional bottom pan. Explore mode previews each part's name and description; quiz mode hides the labels and describes each part by its job, with two attempts, a hint after the first miss and mastery at 5 of 6 on the first attempt.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Fan base types: unitary, isolation and inertia bases
learningObjectives: The learner will identify the unitary, isolation and inertia bases, the spring isolators, the reinforcing rods (rebar) and the bottom pan on FanPedia's base drawings, given each part's function.

accessibility.notes: The drawing is a labelled SVG group; every numbered marker is a focusable role=button and Tab walks them in number order; Enter or Space selects one; focus or hover previews its name and description. During the quiz the markers are named only 'Part n' until resolved, labels and leader lines are hidden, and hints never name the answer. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an 'Answer' badge pair with colour. Text is 12 px or larger; markers keep a constant pixel size; the label column moves below the drawing on narrow screens.

simulation.modelType: labeled diagram with locate quiz (FP.Overlay callout engine on FP.CalloutQuiz)
rules: Explore mode: hover or focus previews a part's name and description; click, Enter or Space opens it and counts it as visited; never scored.
Quiz mode: 6 prompts in a seeded shuffle (the same order for every learner; Start over reshuffles).
Two attempts per prompt; the first wrong answer shows a hint that does not name the answer; the second reveals the answer and counts as missed.
Selecting empty space uses no attempt.
Only first-attempt answers count toward mastery; mastery is 5 of 6.
assumptions: FanPedia pp. 131-132 base type drawings with the printed labels removed and the two p. 132 drawings placed below the p. 131 drawings; marker positions are percentages of the image.
limitations: The drawings are FanPedia's, not a specific current catalog model; the fans in the top row and the base under the bottom-right fan carry no marker; rubber-in-shear isolators are named in the descriptions but not shown.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labelled markers on the real FanPedia drawing first, then retrieval practice: find each part from a description of its job, with a hint after the first miss and immediate correction.
keyQuestions: Which base is designed for use without isolators?
What does an inertia base add to an isolation base, and who supplies the concrete?
commonMisconceptions: Any fan base can go on isolators.
An inertia base ships full of concrete.
An inertia base is a different kind of frame from an isolation base.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 6'; mastery is 5 of 6 on the first attempt.
